Λέγε, φησίν. Κύριε, φημί, εἰ γυναῖκα ἔχων τις πιστὴν ἐν Κυρίῳ [καὶ] ταύτην εὕρῃ ἐν μοιχείᾳ τινί, ἆρα ἁμαρτάνει ὁ ἀνὴρ συνζῶν μετ᾿ αὐτῆς; 5. Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας, φησίν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· ἐὰν δὲ γνῷ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτῆς, καὶ μὴ μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνή, ἀλλ᾿ ἐπιμένῃ τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ μετ᾿ αὐτῆς, ἔνοχος γίνεται τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῆς καὶ κοινωνὸς τῆς μοιχείας αὐτῆς. 6. Τί οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ποιήσῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐὰν ἐπιμείνῃ τῷ πάθει τούτῳ ἡ γυνή; Ἀπολυσάτω, φησίν, αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῷ μενέτω· ἐὰν δὲ ἀπολύσας τὴν γυναῖκα ἑτέραν γαμήσῃ, καὶ αὐτὸς μοιχᾶται. 7. Ἐὰν οὖν, φημί, κύριε, μετὰ τὸ ἀπολυθῆναι τὴν γυναῖκα μετανοήσῃ [ἡ γυνὴ] καὶ θελήσῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἑαυτῆς ἄνδρα ὑποστρέψαι, οὐ παραδεχθήσεται; 8. Καὶ μήν, φησίν, ἐὰν μὴ παραδέξηται αὐτὴν ὁ ἀνήρ, ἁμαρτάνει καὶ μεγάλην ἁμαρτίαν ἑαυτῷ ἐπισπᾶται, ἀλλὰ δεῖ παραδεχθῆναι τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα καὶ μετανοοῦντα· μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ δέ· τοῖς γὰρ δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία. διὰ τὴν μετάνοιαν οὖν οὐκ ὀφείλει γαμεῖν ὁ ἀνήρ. αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις ἐπὶ γυναικὶ καὶ ἀνδρὶ κεῖται. 9. οὐ μόνον, φησί, μοιχεία ἐστίν, ἐάν τις τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ μιάνῃ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃς ἂν τὰ ὁμοιώματα ποιῇ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, μοιχᾶται. ὥστε καὶ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις ἔργοις ἐὰν ἐμμένῃ τις καὶ μὴ μετανοῇ, ἀπέχου ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ συνζῆθι αὐτῷ· εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ μέτοχος εἶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ. 10. διὰ τοῦτο προσετάγη ὑμῖν ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν, εἴτε ἀνὴρ εἴτε γυνή· δύναται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις μετάνοια εἶναι. 11. ἐγὼ οὖν, φησίν, οὐ δίδωμι ἀφορμὴν ἵνα αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις οὕτως συντελῆται, ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνειν τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα. περὶ δὲ τῆς προτέρας ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ὁ δυνάμενος ἴασιν δοῦναι· αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἔχων πάντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν.

translation.text:
“I am commanding you,” he says, “to guard chastity, and do not let a thought about another man’s wife[1], or about any fornication, or about any such evil likenesses, rise up upon your heart[2]. For in doing this you commit a great sin. But if you remember your own wife always, you will never transgress.

“For if this thought rises up upon your heart, you will transgress—and if other such evil things [do], you commit sin. For this thought is a great sin for a servant of God; and if anyone carries out this evil deed, he brings death upon himself[3]. Look to yourself, then: keep away from this thought; for where modesty dwells, there lawlessness ought not to rise up upon the heart of a righteous man.”

I say to him, “Sir,[4] allow me to ask you a few things.” “Speak,” he says. “Sir,” I say, “if someone has a wife who is faithful in the Lord, and he finds her in some adultery, does the husband sin by living together with her?”

“As long as he is ignorant,” he says, “he does not sin; but if the husband comes to know her sin, and the wife does not repent[b] but persists in her fornication, and the husband lives together with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a sharer in her adultery. "What then, sir," I say, "should the husband do, if the wife persists in this passion?" "Let him divorce her," he says, "and let the husband remain by himself; but if, after divorcing his wife, he marries another, he himself also commits adultery." "If then, sir," I say, "after the wife is divorced, she repents and wishes to return to her own husband, will she not be received?" "Indeed," he says, "if the husband does not receive her, he sins and brings a great sin upon himself; rather, the one who has sinned and is repenting must be received—but not repeatedly[5]—for to the servants of God repentance is one[6]. Because of repentance, then, the man ought not to marry. This rule is laid upon both woman and man.

“Not only,” he says, “is it adultery if someone defiles his flesh, but whoever makes images as the nations do[8] is committing adultery. Therefore, even in such works, if someone persists and does not repent, keep away from him and do not live together with him; otherwise you too are a sharer in his sin. For this reason it was commanded you to remain by yourselves[7], whether man or woman, for in cases like these there can be repentance.

“I therefore,” he says, “do not give an occasion for this practice to be carried through in this way, but so that the one who has sinned may no longer sin. But with regard to his former sin, there is One who is able to give healing[9]—for he is the One who has authority over all.”

footnotes.text: “Another man’s wife” (γυναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας) is a common idiom for a woman belonging to another, i.e., a married woman not one’s own.
The phrase “rise up upon the heart” reflects the Greek idiom ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν, a vivid picture of a thought’s ascent into the inner life.
“Brings death upon himself” translates κατεργάζομαι + θάνατος; alternatively, “works out death for himself.”
Rendered “Sir” (Κύριε) to reflect respectful address to the shepherd; alternatively “Lord.”
“Not repeatedly” (μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ) could also be read “not for long,” but the context (μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία, “repentance is one”) suggests limitation of frequency rather than duration.
“Repentance is one” echoes Hermas’s distinctive teaching about a single decisive repentance after grave sin; cf. its reception in later penitential discipline.
“To remain by yourselves” (ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν) idiomatically means to remain unmarried/single in this context, preserving space for the other’s repentance.
“Makes images as the nations do” (τὰ ὁμοιώματα ποιῇ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν) points to idol-making; Hermas labels such idolatry as ‘adultery’ in a covenantal sense (cf. Rom 1:23 for ὁμοίωμα with images).

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

The working Greek includes the ability to give healing. Sinaiticus’s first-hand text proceeds directly to the one who has authority; its corrections ca and d supply the healing clause (project XML, Hermas 29.11). Lake’s Athos transcription, Plate V line 32, and the Latin Vulgata (Hilgenfeld 1873, printed p. 40) also include healing. These are bounded transcription/edition comparisons, not a fresh collation of all manuscript photographs.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally excellent and handles Hermas's moral register well. I have flagged a few minor issues primarily related to consistency in translating repeated idioms (ἀναβαίνω ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν and ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζομαι) and smoothed out a couple of awkward literalisms in verse 5.
issues_found: Inconsistency: The idiom ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν is translated three different ways in three consecutive verses ('rise up', 'climbs up', 'arise'). It should be harmonized to 'rise up upon the heart' throughout.
Inconsistency: ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζομαι is translated as 'commit a great sin' in v. 1 but 'doing sin' in v. 2. Harmonized to 'commit sin' in v. 2.
Awkward English: In v. 5, 'Up to the point of ignorance' is an overly literal rendering of Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας. 'As long as he is ignorant' captures the temporal state more naturally.
Awkward English: In v. 5, 'for for the slaves of God' creates a stuttering repetition. Changed to 'for to the slaves of God' (τοῖς γὰρ δούλοις).

source.text: Ἐντέλλομαί σοι, φησίν, φυλάσσειν τὴν ἁγνείαν καὶ μὴ ἀναβαινέτω σου ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν περὶ γυναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας ἢ περὶ πορνείας τινὸς ἢ περὶ τοιούτων τινῶν ὁμοιωμάτων πονηρῶν. τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν μεγάλην ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζῃ. τῆς δὲ σῆς μνημονεύων πάντοτε γυναικὸς οὐδέποτε διαμαρτήσεις. 2. ἐὰν γὰρ αὕτη ἡ ἐνθύμησις ἐπὶ [τὴν] καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, διαμαρτήσεις, καὶ ἐὰν ἕτερα οὕτως πονηρά, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζῃ· ἡ γὰρ ἐνθύμησις αὕτη Θεοῦ δούλῳ ἁμαρτία μεγάλη ἐστίν· ἐὰν δέ τις ἐργάσηται τὸ ἔργον τὸ πονηρὸν τοῦτο, θάνατον ἑαυτῷ κατεργάζεται. 3. βλέπε οὖν σύ· ἀπέχου ἀπὸ τῆς ἐνθυμήσεως ταύτης· ὅπου γὰρ σεμνότης κατοικεῖ, ἐκεῖ ἀνομία οὐκ ὀφείλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνδρὸς δικαίου. 4. λέγω αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ὀλίγα ἐπερωτῆσαί σε. Λέγε, φησίν. Κύριε, φημί, εἰ γυναῖκα ἔχων τις πιστὴν ἐν Κυρίῳ [καὶ] ταύτην εὕρῃ ἐν μοιχείᾳ τινί, ἆρα ἁμαρτάνει ὁ ἀνὴρ συνζῶν μετ᾿ αὐτῆς; 5. Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας, φησίν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· ἐὰν δὲ γνῷ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτῆς, καὶ μὴ μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνή, ἀλλ᾿ ἐπιμένῃ τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ μετ᾿ αὐτῆς, ἔνοχος γίνεται τῆς ἁ δεχθῆναι τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα καὶ μετανοοῦντα· μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ δέ· τοῖς γὰρ δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία. διὰ τὴν μετάνοιαν οὖν οὐκ ὀφείλει γαμεῖν ὁ ἀνήρ. αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις ἐπὶ γυναικὶ καὶ ἀνδρὶ κεῖται. 9. οὐ μόνον, φησί, μοιχεία ἐστίν, ἐάν τις τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ μιάνῃ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃς ἂν τὰ ὁμοιώματα ποιῇ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, μοιχᾶται. ὥστε καὶ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις ἔργοις ἐὰν ἐμμένῃ τις καὶ μὴ μετανοῇ, ἀπέχου ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ συνζῆθι αὐτῷ· εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ μέτοχος εἶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ. 10. διὰ τοῦτο προσετάγη ὑμῖν ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν, εἴτε ἀνὴρ εἴτε γυνή· δύναται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις μετάνοια εἶναι. 11. ἐγὼ οὖν, φησίν, οὐ δίδωμι ἀφορμὴν ἵνα αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις οὕτως συντελῆται, ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνειν τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα. περὶ δὲ τῆς προτέρας ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ὁ δυνάμενος ἴασιν δοῦναι· αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἔχων πάντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν.

translation.text: “I am commanding you,” he says, “to guard chastity, and do not let a thought about another man’s wife, or about any fornication, or about any such evil likenesses, rise up upon your heart. For in doing this you commit a great sin. But if you remember your own wife always, you will never transgress.

translation.text: “For if this thought rises up upon your heart, you will transgress—and if other such evil things [do], you commit sin. For this thought is a great sin for a servant of God; and if anyone carries out this evil deed, he brings death upon himself. Look to yourself, then: keep away from this thought; for where modesty dwells, there lawlessness ought not to rise up upon the heart of a righteous man.”

translation.text: I say to him, “Sir, allow me to ask you a few things.” “Speak,” he says. “Sir,” I say, “if someone has a wife who is faithful in the Lord, and he finds her in some adultery, does the husband sin by living together with her?”

source.text: Ἐντέλλομαί σοι, φησίν, φυλάσσειν τὴν ἁγνείαν καὶ μὴ ἀναβαινέτω σου ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν περὶ γυναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας ἢ περὶ πορνείας τινὸς ἢ περὶ τοιούτων τινῶν ὁμοιωμάτων πονηρῶν. τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν μεγάλην ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζῃ. τῆς δὲ σῆς μνημονεύων πάντοτε γυναικὸς οὐδέποτε διαμαρτήσεις. 2. ἐὰν γὰρ αὕτη ἡ ἐνθύμησις ἐπὶ [τὴν] καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, διαμαρτήσεις, καὶ ἐὰν ἕτερα οὕτως πονηρά, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζῃ· ἡ γὰρ ἐνθύμησις αὕτη Θεοῦ δούλῳ ἁμαρτία μεγάλη ἐστίν· ἐὰν δέ τις ἐργάσηται τὸ ἔργον τὸ πονηρὸν τοῦτο, θάνατον ἑαυτῷ κατεργάζεται. 3. βλέπε οὖν σύ· ἀπέχου ἀπὸ τῆς ἐνθυμήσεως ταύτης· ὅπου γὰρ σεμνότης κατοικεῖ, ἐκεῖ ἀνομία οὐκ ὀφείλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνδρὸς δικαίου. 4. λέγω αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ὀλίγα ἐπερωτῆσαί σε. Λέγε, φησίν. Κύριε, φημί, εἰ γυναῖκα ἔχων τις πιστὴν ἐν Κυρίῳ [καὶ] ταύτην εὕρῃ ἐν μοιχείᾳ τινί, ἆρα ἁμαρτάνει ὁ ἀνὴρ συνζῶν μετ᾿ αὐτῆς; 5. Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας, φησίν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· ἐὰν δὲ γνῷ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτῆς, καὶ μὴ μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνή, ἀλλ᾿ ἐπιμένῃ τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ μετ᾿ αὐτῆς, ἔνοχος γίνεται τῆς ἁ δεχθῆναι τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα καὶ μετανοοῦντα· μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ δέ· τοῖς γὰρ δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία. διὰ τὴν μετάνοιαν οὖν οὐκ ὀφείλει γαμεῖν ὁ ἀνήρ. αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις ἐπὶ γυναικὶ καὶ ἀνδρὶ κεῖται. 9. οὐ μόνον, φησί, μοιχεία ἐστίν, ἐάν τις τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ μιάνῃ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃς ἂν τὰ ὁμοιώματα ποιῇ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, μοιχᾶται. ὥστε καὶ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις ἔργοις ἐὰν ἐμμένῃ τις καὶ μὴ μετανοῇ, ἀπέχου ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ συνζῆθι αὐτῷ· εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ μέτοχος εἶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ. 10. διὰ τοῦτο προσετάγη ὑμῖν ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν, εἴτε ἀνὴρ εἴτε γυνή· δύναται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις μετάνοια εἶναι. 11. ἐγὼ οὖν, φησίν, οὐ δίδωμι ἀφορμὴν ἵνα αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις οὕτως συντελῆται, ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνειν τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα. περὶ δὲ τῆς προτέρας ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ὁ δυνάμενος ἴασιν δοῦναι· αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἔχων πάντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν.

translation.text: “As long as he is ignorant,” he says, “he does not sin; but if the husband comes to know her sin, and the wife does not repent[a] but persists in her fornication, and the husband lives together with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a sharer in her adultery. "What then, sir," I say, "should the husband do, if the wife persists in this passion?" "Let him divorce her," he says, "and let the husband remain by himself; but if, after divorcing his wife, he marries another, he himself also commits adultery." "If then, sir," I say, "after the wife is divorced, she repents and wishes to return to her own husband, will she not be received?" "Indeed," he says, "if the husband does not receive her, he sins and brings a great sin upon himself; rather, the one who has sinned and is repenting must be received—but not repeatedly—for to the servants of God repentance is one. Because of repentance, then, the man ought not to marry. This rule is laid upon both woman and man.

translation.text: “Not only,” he says, “is it adultery if someone defiles his flesh, but whoever makes images as the nations do is committing adultery. Therefore, even in such works, if someone persists and does not repent[a], keep away from him and do not live together with him; otherwise you too are a sharer in his sin. For this reason it was commanded you to remain by yourselves, whether man or woman, for in cases like these there can be repentance.

Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας, φησίν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· ἐὰν δὲ γνῷ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτῆς, καὶ μὴ μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνή, ἀλλ᾿ ἐπιμένῃ τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ μετ᾿ αὐτῆς, ἔνοχος γίνεται τῆς ἁ δεχθῆναι τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα καὶ μετανοοῦντα· μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ δέ· τοῖς γὰρ δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία. διὰ τὴν μετάνοιαν οὖν οὐκ ὀφείλει γαμεῖν ὁ ἀνήρ. αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις ἐπὶ γυναικὶ καὶ ἀνδρὶ κεῖται. 9. οὐ μόνον, φησί, μοιχεία ἐστίν, ἐάν τις τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ μιάνῃ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃς ἂν τὰ ὁμοιώματα ποιῇ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, μοιχᾶται. ὥστε καὶ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις ἔργοις ἐὰν ἐμμένῃ τις καὶ μὴ μετανοῇ, ἀπέχου ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ συνζῆθι αὐτῷ· εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ μέτοχος εἶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ. 10. διὰ τοῦτο προσετάγη ὑμῖν ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν, εἴτε ἀνὴρ εἴτε γυνή· δύναται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις μετάνοια εἶναι. 11. ἐγὼ οὖν, φησίν, οὐ δίδωμι ἀφορμὴν ἵνα αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις οὕτως συντελῆται, ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνειν τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα. περὶ δὲ τῆς προτέρας ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ὁ δυνάμενος ἴασιν δοῦναι· αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἔχων πάντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν.

base_translation.text: “As long as he is ignorant,” he says, “he does not sin; but if the husband comes to know her sin, and the wife does not repent but persists in her fornication, and the husband lives together with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a sharer in her adultery. "What then, sir," I say, "should the husband do, if the wife persists in this passion?" "Let him divorce her," he says, "and let the husband remain by himself; but if, after divorcing his wife, he marries another, he himself also commits adultery." "If then, sir," I say, "after the wife is divorced, she repents and wishes to return to her own husband, will she not be received?" "Indeed," he says, "if the husband does not receive her, he sins and brings a great sin upon himself; rather, the one who has sinned and is repenting must be received—but not repeatedly—for to the slaves of God repentance is one. Because of repentance, then, the man ought not to marry. This rule is laid upon both woman and man.

translation.text:
“As long as the husband does not know,” he says, “he does not sin. But if he learns of his wife’s sin, and she refuses to repent[a] and continues in sexual immorality, then, if he continues living with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and shares in her adultery.”

“What should the husband do, then, sir,” I ask, “if his wife continues in this sinful behavior?”

“He should divorce her,” he says, “and remain unmarried. If he divorces his wife and marries another woman, he also commits adultery.”

“But sir,” I ask, “suppose the divorced wife repents and wants to return to her husband. Should he not take her back?”

“He certainly should,” he says. “If her husband refuses to take her back, he sins and brings a serious sin upon himself. A person who has sinned and is repenting must be received—but not repeatedly, for God’s servants have one repentance. Therefore, because she may repent, the husband must not marry another woman. This rule applies equally to women and men.”

base_translation.text: “Not only,” he says, “is it adultery if someone defiles his flesh, but whoever makes images as the nations do is committing adultery. Therefore, even in such works, if someone persists and does not repent, keep away from him and do not live together with him; otherwise you too are a sharer in his sin. For this reason it was commanded you to remain by yourselves, whether man or woman, for in cases like these there can be repentance.

translation.text: “Adultery,” he says, “is not only a matter of defiling one’s own body. Anyone who makes images as pagan peoples do is also committing adultery. So if someone continues to do such things and does not repent[a], stay away from that person and do not live with them. Otherwise, you too will share in their sin. This is why a man or woman who separates was commanded to remain unmarried: repentance is still possible in such cases.”

base_translation.text: “I therefore,” he says, “do not give an occasion for this practice to be carried through in this way, but so that the one who has sinned may no longer sin. footnotes.text: “Another man’s wife” (γυναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας) is a common idiom for a woman belonging to another, i.e., a married woman not one’s own.
The phrase “rise up upon the heart” reflects the Greek idiom ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν, a vivid picture of a thought’s ascent into the inner life.
“Brings death upon himself” translates κατεργάζομαι + θάνατος; alternatively, “works out death for himself.”
Rendered “Sir” (Κύριε) to reflect respectful address to the shepherd; alternatively “Lord.”
“Not repeatedly” (μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ) could also be read “not for long,” but the context (μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία, “repentance is one”) suggests limitation of frequency rather than duration.
“Repentance is one” echoes Hermas’s distinctive teaching about a single decisive repentance after grave sin; cf. its reception in later penitential discipline.
“To remain by yourselves” (ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν) idiomatically means to remain unmarried/single in this context, preserving space for the other’s repentance.

Or 'he becomes guilty of her sin. Let the one who has sinned and is repenting be received'.

I say to him, “Sir, allow me to ask you a few things.” “Speak,” he says. “Sir,” I say, “if someone has a wife who is faithful in the Lord, and he finds her in some adultery, does the husband sin by living together with her?”

“Not repeatedly” (μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ) could also be read “not for long,” but the context (μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία, “repentance is one”) suggests limitation of frequency rather than duration.
